case.title: Mr. Bernard Enya Edu v. Cross River University of Technology (CRUTECH) & Ors
defendants: The Vice-Chancellor, Cross River University of Technology (CRUTECH)
The Governing Council, Cross River University of Technology (CRUTECH)

procedural_history.originating_proceedings: Complaint filed on 18th January 2013; amended complaint filed on 15th May 2013.
procedural_history.procedural_posture: Preliminary objection challenging jurisdiction on grounds that action is statute barred and abuse of court process.
interlocutory_applications: Notice of Preliminary Objection filed by defendants on 14th May 2013.
procedural_events: Defendants entered conditional appearance on 14th May 2013.

material_facts: Claimant was compulsorily retired by the 1st defendant on 4th January 2012.
Claimant petitioned the Cross River State House of Assembly regarding his compulsory retirement.
The House of Assembly passed a resolution on 24th October 2012 upholding the defendants' action.

chronology.event: Cross River State House of Assembly passed resolution affirming defendants' action.
Claimant filed complaint at National Industrial Court.

admitted_facts: Both parties agree that the defendants are all Public Officers.
disputed_facts: Whether the cause of action arose on 4th January 2012 or 24th October 2012.
Whether the Public Officers Protection Law applies to the claimant's contract of employment.
facts.employment_relationship: Claimant was employed as a lecturer and director of CRUTECH Entrepreneurial Centre by the 1st defendant.
facts.contractual_relationship: Contract of employment between claimant and 1st defendant.

claims.claim: Declaration that compulsory retirement is illegal, unconstitutional, null and void.
Mandatory injunction for reinstatement to employment and positions.
Mandatory injunction for payment of arrears of entitlements and promotions.
Perpetual injunction restraining defendants from compulsorily retiring claimant without due process.
General damages of N45,000,000.00 for difficulties and psychological trauma.
Exemplary damages of N4,500,000.00 for conduct of defendants.
Cost of N5,000,000.00 for prosecution of suit.

reliefs_sought.relief: Declaration that purported compulsory retirement is illegal, unconstitutional, null and void.
Mandatory injunction for reinstatement to employment and positions.
Mandatory injunction for payment of arrears of entitlements and promotions.
Perpetual injunction restraining defendants from compulsorily retiring claimant without due process.

issues_for_determination.issue: Whether the action is statute barred having regards to section 1A of the Cross River State Public Officers Protection Law.
Whether the suit is an abuse of court process as it is statute barred and brought in a court without jurisdiction.
Whether the combination of other causes of action outside jurisdiction with one within jurisdiction robs the court of jurisdiction.
Whether the Public Officers Protection Law applies to a suit challenging breach of contract of employment.
Whether time started running from 4th January 2012 or 24th October 2012.
Whether there is any claim on defamation before the court.

questions_of_law: Applicability of the Public Officers Protection Law to employment contracts.
Computation of limitation period for statute-barred actions.

claimant_arguments: The Public Officers Protection Law does not apply to a suit founded on contract of employment.
The cause of action arose on 24th October 2012 when the House of Assembly passed a resolution, not on 4th January 2012.
There is no claim on defamation before the court.
defendant_arguments: The action is statute barred as it was filed outside the six months period allowed by section 1A of the Public Officers Protection Law.
The suit is an abuse of court process.
The combination of causes of action outside jurisdiction robs the court of jurisdiction.
The defendants are Public Officers protected by the Public Officers Protection Law.

findings_of_fact.issue: Date of accrual of cause of action
findings_of_fact.finding: Cause of action arose on 4th January 2012 when the letter of compulsory retirement was written.

findings_of_law.issue: Applicability of Public Officers Protection Law
findings_of_law.finding: The Public Officers Protection Law applies to the claimant's employment contract as it is an action for illegal compulsory retirement.
The action is statute barred as it was filed outside the six months period.

judicial_analysis.reasoning: The court considered the submissions and authorities. It held that the cause of action arose on 4th January 2012, and the suit filed on 18th January 2013 was outside the six months limitation period under the Public Officers Protection Law. The petition to the House of Assembly did not stop the limitation period from running. The court found that the action is statute barred and lacks jurisdiction.

issue_analysis.issue: Whether the action is statute barred having regards to section 1A of the Cross River State Public Officers Protection Law.

arguments.claimant: The Public Officers Protection Law does not apply to contract of employment; cause of action arose on 24th October 2012.
arguments.defendant: The action is statute barred as it was filed outside six months from 4th January 2012.

issue_analysis.judicial_analysis: The court found that the cause of action arose on 4th January 2012 and the suit was filed on 18th January 2013, outside the six months period. The petition to the House of Assembly did not affect the limitation period.
issue_analysis.ratio_decidendi: An action against a public officer for acts done in pursuance of public duty must be commenced within six months of the accrual of the cause of action.

holdings.issue: Whether the action is statute barred
holdings.holding: The action is statute barred and the court lacks jurisdiction.

ratio_decidendi.issue: Limitation period under Public Officers Protection Law
ratio_decidendi.principle: Actions against public officers for acts done in pursuance of public duty must be instituted within six months of the accrual of the cause of action.
ratio_decidendi.application: The claimant's action was filed more than six months after the compulsory retirement.

legal_principles.principle: Statute of limitation bars actions not brought within the prescribed period.
legal_principles.source: Section 1(a) of the Public Officers Protection Law Cap P17 Laws of Cross River State 2004 as amended.

statutory_interpretation.statute: Public Officers Protection Law Cap P17 Laws of Cross River State 2004 as amended
statutory_interpretation.interpretation: Actions against public officers must be commenced within six months of the act complained of.
statutory_interpretation.application: The claimant's action was filed outside the six months period.

precedent_analysis.proposition: Action for wrongful dismissal was caught by the Public Officers Protection Act.
precedent_analysis.reasoning: The Supreme Court held that the action was statute barred.
